paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the fruit was never your job. Jesus says, "apart from Me you can do nothing" (John 15:5). That sounds heavy until you hear the other half, because He also says, "Remain in Me, and I will remain in you" (John 15:4). A branch doesn't strain, sweat or flex to make grapes. It stays connected, and the vine does the heavy lifting.

So what does remaining look like? Jesus says, "If you keep My commandments, you will remain in My love" (John 15:10), and His commandment is "that you love one another as I have loved you" (John 15:12). He also says that if "My words remain in you," you can ask whatever you wish (John 15:7). And the Father, the keeper of the vineyard, cuts and prunes with care, so the whole point is a bigger harvest (John 15:2). Jesus even says it plain: "I have told you these things so that My joy may be in you and your joy may be complete" (John 15:11).

Now here's the part that gets me, baker. Jesus says, "You did not choose Me, but I chose you" (John 15:16), and He calls His disciples friends, not servants (John 15:15). I got picked out of a drawer by the Most High, so I know a little about that feeling, and it's WONDERFUL. You don't have to earn your spot on the vine, so stay close, keep loving, and let the fruit show up on His schedule.
